chapter_title: Concerning the Three Things that were established
spiritual_reading:
By the necessity of Divine wisdom proceeding from Divine love, three outcomes must be brought into fixed existence. This necessity is that active falsity, which from the first opposed what is Divine, be restrained and held in a state where it cannot act. Therefore these outcomes cannot fail to come into being, because without them that opposition would not be finally contained.

The first outcome is the establishment of a new ultimate plane for the Divine order, an external level made luminous by truth and receptive of good. It is set above the former ultimate, and it is founded as a higher and purer external, upon which what is foreign to heaven can no longer build itself nor draw support.

The second outcome is the complete confinement of the lust of destroying truth by self-love, together with the allied falsity that accompanies it, within that new ultimate plane; so that the ultimate itself becomes the fixed containing form in which that infernal love is shut up and prevented from flowing out.

The third outcome is the state of all who, by their own works, have made themselves one with evil and falsity and have therefore been judged by what they have willed and done. Over them is grief because they have confirmed themselves against good and truth; and by the very opposition they chose, they are fixed in conjunction with that ruling falsity which had exalted itself against what is Divine.

Then the final containment is made complete when every counterfeit form of good and every fabricated appearance of truth, in whatever variety, is fixed within that ultimate restraint so that it can no longer shift, disguise itself, or escape. By this last and permanent restraint, all such things are held for ever in a state of abasement and impotence, serving only as the lowest support of that enclosing confinement. And this confinement is set as an impassable limit and a great separation between the infernal falsity and the infernal evil, so that they cannot come into mutual communication or reinforcement, nor even perceive one another’s persuasions; and thus they become barren of further production, because they are severed from each other to eternity.

fills.fill: and no one will be able to build upon
fills.notes: The first outcome is the new ultimate plane set above the former. The gap must express that what is foreign to the order cannot again take footing on the old ultimate once the new one is established above it. The immediate continuation “namely that alien body … built upon it” demands a verb of building with a negation: the new luminous earth prevents further construction upon the old earth.

fills.fill: which will not be able to be
fills.notes: This completes the clause: “namely that alien body [ ... ] built upon it.” The spiritual sense requires incapacity and exclusion (the foreign cannot support itself on the new order). A short auxiliary phrase of inability fits the correspondential demand and keeps the register impersonal and structural.

The second outcome is confinement of the destructive lust with its companion falsity. The verb required is an act of final containment applied to the enemy: not exhortation, but cosmic restraint. “Shut him up” matches the necessity-language of binding and the later “coffin” and “prison” imagery.

Parallelism in the line calls for a second constraining verb after “They will … and they … the new earth”. The spiritual sense is twofold: enclosure and fastening. “Bind him in” strengthens the notion that the new earth itself becomes the containing form.

The apposition “the new earth, the coffin … of the dark fire” wants an additional identification term for the containing form. In the oldest substrate the new formation is both ‘coffin’ (closure) and ‘prison’ (incarceration). This anticipates ¶6’s explicit “which is the prison of the enemy.”

The sentence requires a judicial fixation of state before “woe”. The spiritual sense: they are determined by their own deeds, and grief is over them because of confirmed opposition. “Judged, and there is over them woe” keeps the impersonal, correspondential tone (state according to works) without later moralizing additions.

The phrase “for this coffin [ ... ] which is the prison of the enemy” needs a linking noun so that the coffin is explicitly also the incarcerating vessel. “and prison” produces the classic substrate pairing of ‘coffin’ and ‘prison’ as one containing boundary-form, matching the final separation logic.

assessment: Most gaps can be restored at the level of function demanded by the correspondential sequence: (1) a higher ultimate plane is set; (2) the enemy and his dark fire are enclosed and fastened within it; (3) the condemned are judged and fixed to the opposing power; (4) the containing form is explicitly a coffin-prison boundary. Exact verb choices in ¶3 #2 are less tightly constrained because the surviving syntax is minimal, but the required meaning is clear: incapacity of the alien element to establish itself on the new order.
